spec_section: §1 D1 (expand's per-node cap excludes seed atoms) / §3.5,§3.9
query: how do we escalate a production incident
gap_reason: D1 (§1): the legacy-incident-escalation reef has 12 linked corals, above MAX_SIBLING_ATOMS_PER_NODE=10, so its supersession annotation depends on Store::expand's seeds-first guarantee -- d1a01 (the seed this query retrieves directly) must survive the per-node cap, and its 9 filler siblings must be chosen by query-cosine similarity, or the x0.5 supersession penalty never applies and d1a01 could outrank d1b01 (current). Verified by temporarily reverting Store::expand's Postgres SQL to the pre-D1 'ORDER BY na.atom_id LIMIT 10' cap (no seed priority) and re-running 6 times (fresh random graph_id/atom_id permutation each run): this case's own rank_before held in all 6 runs regardless (with 12 atoms and cap 10, a specific seed survives the naive cap by pure luck ~83% of the time, which is what was observed) -- so on its own this case is a REAL but only probabilistically-triggered D1 regression guard. The companion native check in this file (escalation_reef_expand_d1_native_checks, assertion (b): expand()'s filler selection must equal the independently-recomputed top-9-by-cosine-similarity set) is the reliable one -- it failed 5 of the same 6 pre-D1 runs, because matching the true similarity order by atom_id luck alone is a much narrower target than merely including one specific atom. Together they cover both the probabilistic (case-level) and near-deterministic (native, order-exact) faces of the same D1 guarantee.
